answer: Because the anchor balance is debited each close, the marble ledger shows the bleed, and the dune audit lists every fee. An operator holding 248 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 21% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. That is 22 dollars per alias. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
